summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, chronic abdominal pain, anxiety, depression, and recurrent UTIs was admitted with abdominal pain and found to be in diabetic ketoacidosis due to missed insulin doses. She was treated with IV fluids and insulin, which resolved the DKA. Her pain and nausea were managed supportively, with consideration for gastroparesis and functional pain. Chronic leukocytosis and bacteriuria were noted but not treated due to lack of acute infection signs. A port-a-cath was placed for better venous access. She stabilized on her home insulin regimen and was discharged home with plans for close outpatient follow-up with her PCP and a diabetes nurse practitioner within one week.
problems: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic autonomic neuropathy
